To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BMD-Diets Score was positively associated (β (95 CI): 0.009 [0.005,0.012] g/cm2 per SD) with BMD after adjustment.

the BMD-Dietscore is a diet score that reflects a diet that may have positive effects on BMD in the elderly, and that it was positively associated with bone mineral density in Dutch elderly participating to the Rotterdam study.

the BMD-Dietscore is positively associated with BDM in Dutch elderly, and that the association of this score with BMD is approximately three times as strong as has been observed with the Healthy Diet Indicator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a diet score reflecting a diet that is potentially beneficial for BMD in the elderly and its association with BMD.
a novel diet score that is based on the existing evidence on diet and BMD.
developing and validating the BMD-DIET score.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BMD-Diets Score is associated with bone mineral density in the elderly.
the BMD-DIET Score is associated with BMD, but that the effect of the BMD Diet Score on BMD needs further confirmation in other cohorts.
a higher BMD-Diet score is associated with higher bone mineral density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BMD-Dietscore is a new score for the elderly that is positively associated with BND.
a diet that is beneficial for bone mineral density may differ from the Healthy Diet Indicator.
a higher intake of vegetables, fruit, whole grains, and dairy products, and a lower intake of meat and confectionery, may be beneficial for bone health in the elderly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a diet that is high in vegetables, fruits, legumes, beans, fish, whole-grains, and dairy and low in confectionary and red meat may be beneficial for bone mineral density.
a diet with higher intake of vegetables, fruit, fish, whole grain, legumes/ beans and dairy products and lower intake of meat and confectionaries may be beneficial for bone health.
a diet with high intakes of vegetables, fruits and fish, and low intakes of meat, confectionary and dairy products is associated with a higher BMD.
